messages.content: Can you settle the fare comparison? The $598 option is vague about a carry-on and choosing a seat, and the other itinerary is now showing $644.

The $598 basic fare includes one standard carry-on, so there is no bag charge. It does not include advance seat selection; available standard seats are $35 each way, adding $70 round trip. That makes its usable total $668. The $644 fare includes both a standard carry-on and advance standard-seat selection.
So the $644 flight is actually cheaper for what I need, even though the headline price is higher?

Yes. On an equivalent basis, the $644 itinerary is $24 less than the $668 basic-fare option. I’d move the $644 round trip into the lead position. Both still work with the workshop schedule, including the 3:15 p.m. Thursday departure from the client site, and nothing has been booked.
